subject.title: fix(gateway): keep failed account stops from stranding siblings

question: Should OpenClaw retain the safety-first failed-stop gate, requiring a later successful teardown before health recovery, reload, or logout can replace or clear the affected account, rather than adopting the restart-after-cleanup behavior proposed by the related PRs?
rationale: The related open PRs address the same failure but intentionally choose a different availability-versus-resource-safety contract; source and tests establish the consequences, but repository owners must choose the permanent operational policy.

options.title: Keep the failed-stop gate
options.body: Merge this safety-first approach after the remaining checks and failed shard are resolved, so a possibly leaked plugin runtime is never overlapped by a replacement.

options.title: Prefer recovery after cleanup
options.body: Rework toward the related approach only if maintainers explicitly accept restart after hook failure and can prove that cleanup makes replacement safe.

recommendation.title: Keep the failed-stop gate
recommendation.body: Merge this safety-first approach after the remaining checks and failed shard are resolved, so a possibly leaked plugin runtime is never overlapped by a replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: This PR defines the current proposed lifecycle contract and associated tests across gateway callers.
